assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

The scenario asserts two user-observable signals: (1) a session row appears in `ready` within 1s of agent launch and (2) the PID is bound within 1s.

**agent = yes.** Hermes Agent v0.19.0 is installed and `hermes chat` is its interactive REPL — the driver launches exactly that under tmux, and the shipped store shows `source='cli'` session rows with `started_at`/`ended_at`/`end_reason` for such runs. Launching in a fresh cwd and idling needs no feature beyond the REPL existing.

**daemon = full.** Hermes is the second `agent.ProcessOwnedStore` adapter after opencode, and opencode's 1.1 cell is recorded and verified 2/2 on the identical transport shape. Both signals are carried by the process scanner, not the store:

- `buildAgentWatchers` gives every ProcessOwnedStore adapter a `processlifecycle.Scanner` alongside its store watcher (wiring.go). Because Hermes' matcher is a `CommandPattern` (a Python console script — `ExactName{"hermes"}` would never fire), the scanner runs `pgrep -f '(^|/)hermes( |$)|hermes_cli\.main'` with the adapter's `ExcludeArgv` filter, which drops the long-lived gateway/serve services but not `chat`.
- On first sight of the PID the scanner mints `proc-<PID>` and emits `EventNewSession` (scanner.go:347) — a `ready` row within one 1s poll tick of launch. `PIDManager` parses the PID straight out of the `proc-<PID>` id (pid_manager.go:719), so PID binding needs no discovery round-trip. This is precisely the path opencode's recording measured at +72ms (birth) / +74ms (pid_discovered).
- The store-backed session follows: Hermes INSERTs the `sessions` row while the session is live, ~2s after launch on the first user message, and the watcher's `scanSessions` (filtered to `source IN ('cli','tui')`, so the messaging-gateway rows are excluded) emits `new_session` + an activity event whose `Terminal` flag comes from `finish_reason='stop'` on the newest assistant row. `findSupersedingSession` then retires the pre-session by PID or adapter+CWD match.

No spec-required observable for this cell is mis-handled, so the verdict stays `full`; the timing and CWD-binding gaps below are caveats, per the caveats-over-downgrades rule.

**driver = ready.** The recipe needs `send`, `wait_turn` and `sleep`; `driver-interactive.sh` declares `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"` and its SEAM 2 polls the store for `finish_reason='stop'` — a real turn-done signal, not an idle heuristic. No primitive is missing.

**No observations block, deliberately.** `of verify`'s metric assertions are checked against the replay golden summary alone, and hermes' tokens/cost cannot reach it: they are computed by `ComputeMetrics` over the SQLite store, a path `cmd/replay` never runs, while hermes' `Parser` contributes only `ModelName`. The store-derived token lift in `cmd/replay/metrics.go` is gated to antigravity. A separate blocker sits upstream of that: the hermes driver reports its transcript as the store URI `<store>?session=<id>`, which `curate-lifecycle-fixture.sh` rejects outright, so no transcript.jsonl and therefore no golden exists at all yet. The two caveats below record both, so the constraint is not rediscovered. This matches the recorded, verified opencode 1.1 sibling, which also asserts phases only. None of this changes the pillars — the phases this cell asserts are lifecycle events from events.jsonl, which are unaffected.

**Provisional, per the observation-vs-emission rule.** Everything above is read off the adapter, the daemon wiring and the maintainer's live store — no recording exists yet. The two things only a recording can settle are whether pre-session birth actually lands inside the 1000 ms budget for this adapter, and whether the pre-session→store-session supersession completes cleanly when the store row carries no cwd. Hence confidence 0.8 rather than higher.
caveats: The <1s birth is satisfied by the `proc-<PID>` pre-session, NOT by Hermes' own store row: the `sessions` row is INSERTed ~2s after launch, on the first user message (adapter.go package doc; foldMessages comment). Same shape as opencode, whose store row landed at +528ms while the pre-session covered the budget.

`sessions.cwd` is populated only by Hermes' tui_gateway, so an interactive `hermes chat` session (source='cli') carries NO cwd — verified: every row in the maintainer's store has an empty cwd. Both the watcher and querySessionMetrics fall back to `defaultLiveCWD`, which deliberately returns "" when zero or more than one live Hermes session process is found. If a second Hermes session is running on the machine during the recording, the store session gets no project binding and the pre-session retirement falls back to the PID match alone.

The process scanner backs off from a 1s to a 5s poll after 5 stable polls (scanner.go:19-20,198-207). On a recording daemon that has been idle before the launch, pre-session birth can therefore exceed the 1000 ms budget. Not Hermes-specific — it is shared by every scanner-backed adapter, including the siblings whose 1.1 recordings pass — but it is the most likely cause if this cell's birth phase verifies late.

NO observations block on the spec, deliberately — `cost_nonzero` and `tokens_nonzero` are UNSATISFIABLE for hermes and would have hard-failed the moment this cell was recorded. `of verify`'s metric assertions (tools/onboarding-factory/internal/validate/observations.go:135-189 ValidateObservations → applyHardAssertions) read ONLY the newest recording's *.replay.json.golden `summary` block. That summary is produced by the offline replay tool, which drives core/pkg/tailer with hermes.Parser (cmd/replay/main.go:86) — and hermes' Parser sets ONLY ev.ModelName (parser.go:77-79); it sets no ev.Tokens and no cost. Hermes' tokens and cost live exclusively in ComputeMetrics' `sessions`-row query (metrics.go:143-163), a path the replay tool never invokes. The one escape hatch — the store-derived token lift in cmd/replay/metrics.go:59 — is gated `if adapter == antigravity.AdapterName`, so hermes' golden would carry cum_input=cum_output=0 and estimated_cost_usd=0. Verified by reading all four files. The recorded, verified opencode 1.1 sibling (the other ProcessOwnedStore adapter) likewise carries no observations block. UPDATE (record, 2026-08-02): still true of cost and tokens, and this recording's golden proves it directly (cum_input=cum_output=0, estimated_cost_usd=0) rather than by reading — but the spec is no longer observation-free: `model` is now pinned and PASSES, so the block exists and asserts exactly one field.

SUPERSEDED (record, 2026-08-02). This caveat's blocker is gone: the driver now DOES dump the store to a synthetic-key JSONL (driver-interactive.sh export_transcript, commit b55e6bb), modelled on opencode's, so a real transcript.jsonl and a real replay golden exist for this cell and ValidateObservations no longer returns Skipped. `model` is pinned from that golden ('gpt-5.6-luna') and verifies green, which is what this caveat asked `record` to do. One sub-claim here was checked and turned out NOT to be a blocker at all: meta.transcript_extensions in replaydata/agents/scenarios.json needs no hermes entry — curate-lifecycle-fixture.sh defaults the extension to "jsonl" (`.meta.transcript_extensions[$a] // "jsonl"`), which is why kiro-cli, gemini-cli, antigravity and mistral-vibe all carry recordings without an entry either. What the export did NOT unlock is tokens and cost: they live on the sessions AGGREGATE row, reachable only through ComputeMetrics, and replay never runs that path.

sources.note: Source = agent.ProcessOwnedStore{PathForPID: StorePath(), Reader: metricsReader{}}; Process.Match = CommandPattern; ExcludeArgv = isServiceArgv; single observe-kind permission "store".

Package doc: no transcript files, one shared state.db; the sessions row is INSERTed ~2s after launch with ended_at NULL; sessions.cwd only for TUI. processCmdPattern + serviceSubcommands exclusion; HERMES_HOME resolution.
scanSessions filters source IN ('cli','tui'), emits new_session then activity; turnIsDone reads finish_reason='stop' on the newest assistant row; TranscriptPath = <store>?session=<id>.

ProcessOwnedStore adapters get their store watcher PLUS a processlifecycle.Scanner; a CommandPattern matcher switches the scanner to pgrep -f and the adapter's ExcludeArgv becomes the scanner's argv filter.
1s default poll (5s after 5 stable polls); maybeTrackNewPID mints proc-<PID> and emits EventNewSession — the row that satisfies the <1s birth.
PID is parsed directly from the proc-<PID> id (no discovery latency); findSupersedingSession retires the pre-session on a PID match, or on adapter+CWD as the fallback.
Sibling ProcessOwnedStore cell, recorded and verified 2/2: pre-session birth +72ms, pid_discovered +74ms, store session +528ms — the same two-phase shape this spec asserts.

DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"; launch seam runs `hermes chat` under tmux and polls for the "Type your message or /help" prompt; wait_turn polls the store for finish_reason='stop'; sqlite3 is a hard prerequisite.

The recording daemon is started via `env <vars> irrlichd --record` without -i, so it inherits HERMES_HOME from the invoking shell — which is what makes daemon and driver agree on which state.db to read.
Upstream project for Hermes Agent; local CLI reports "Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) · upstream 177f1d7c".

12 most recent sessions: all source='cli', cwd empty, model='gpt-5.6-luna', input/output tokens non-zero (e.g. 16269/5), estimated_cost_usd=0.0 with billing_mode='subscription_included', end_reason cli_close/agent_close. The same-second row pairs are two concurrent one-shot runs (distinct prompts 'Say only: alpha' / 'Say only: beta'), not duplicate rows for one launch.

ValidateObservations reads ONLY the newest recording's *.replay.json.golden `summary`; applyHardAssertions checks spec.Model/CostNonzero/TokensNonzero against it. No golden → Skipped(Pass=true), which is why a wrong observations block stays latent until the first recording.

finalizeSummary copies cum tokens/cost/model off the tailer's LastMetrics; the store-derived TotalTokens/ContextWindow lift is gated `if adapter == antigravity.AdapterName` — hermes is excluded, so no store path can reach a hermes golden.

ParseLine sets ev.ModelName (from `_model`) and event/tool fields ONLY — no ev.Tokens, no cost. Contrast opencode/parser.go:148-199 applyStepFinishTokens, which is why opencode's 1.1 golden carries cum_input_tokens=19642.
querySessionMetrics is the ONLY producer of hermes tokens/cost (sessions-row columns + capacity pricing). It runs in the daemon's MetricsProvider path, never in cmd/replay.

curate hard-exits 'transcript not found' unless transcript.path is a real file; the hermes driver writes the store URI '<store>?session=<id>'. opencode dumps the store to a synthetic-key JSONL instead (its driver:929-976) — hermes has no equivalent, so no transcript.jsonl and no golden can be produced yet.

preconditions: hermes >=0.19.0 on PATH and an inference provider configured in <HERMES_HOME>/config.yaml (model.default + model.provider) with working credentials
HERMES_HOME exported in the shell that runs run-cell.sh, so BOTH the recording daemon (which inherits it, spawn-record-daemon.sh) and the driver read the same state.db
sqlite3 on PATH — the store is the only session signal hermes exposes; the driver exits nonzero(2) without it
no other hermes session process running: sessions.cwd is empty for source='cli', so the live-process CWD fallback only binds a project when exactly one session process is alive
irrlichd is recording with the hermes store watcher enabled (grant-all permission mode, so the observe-kind "store" permission is not left pending)

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: events.jsonl contains a hermes session birth (proc-<PID> pre-session or store session) within 1000 ms of agent launch
events.jsonl contains a pid_discovered event within 1000 ms of agent launch
the store-backed session (id <YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>_<hex>) appears and supersedes the pre-session
